title: Is Most-Watched Stock International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) Worth Betting on Now?
detail:
Is Most-Watched Stock International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) Worth Betting on Now?
Zacks Equity Research

IBM
^GSPC
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

IBM (IBM) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this technology and consulting company have returned +9.1%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -5.4% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry, which IBM falls in, has lost 34.2%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, IBM is expected to post earnings of $4.63 per share, indicating a change of +2.4% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.7% over the last 30 days.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $12.41 points to a change of +7.1% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +0.6%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $13.24 indicates a change of +6.7% from what IBM is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.3%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, IBM is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Johnson & Johnson: A Dividend King Guiding Past $100 Billion

Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) pays $1.34 per quarter, or $5.36 annualized, for a forward yield of 1.95% at a share price near $274.54. That is the lowest yield on this list, and it reflects a stock that has gained 34.8% this year. J&J earns its spot on safety.

Dividend safety: The board raised the payout 3.1% in April 2026, which the company marked as its 64th consecutive year of increases (a streak that puts it in rare company, the same 50-plus-year club we ranked by valuation in a free Dividend Kings report). The payment history backs that up, with the quarterly rate climbing every year from $0.90 in 2019 to today's $1.34. Against the midpoint of 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $11.60 to $11.75, the annual dividend uses roughly 46% of earnings, leaving plenty of room for raise number 65.

title: How Much Could You Lose In Rigetti Computing Stock?
detail:
How Much Could You Lose In Rigetti Computing Stock?
Trefis Team

Shares of Rigetti Computing (RGTI) lost 32.5% over the month to November 5, 2026. The S&P 500 fell 5.7% over the same period, while peers IonQ and D-Wave Quantum fell even more than Rigetti. The stock ended that day at $9.85, marking its lowest close of the past year. If the wider market turns lower from here, how much more could Rigetti shareholders lose? A repeat of the stock's average sell-off fall of 52.2% would take it from $9.85 to about $4.71.

How Far Has Rigetti Stock Fallen In Past Sell-Offs?

Rigetti stock has dropped much further than the S&P 500 during every market sell-off since the company began trading in March 2022. For 2022, the comparison dates start on March 2, its first trading day, although the broader sell-off began in early January. The stock suffered its largest decline during the 2022 inflation and Fed tightening shock, losing 83% compared with a 17.6% drop for the S&P 500. A portion of that decline occurred on September 6, 2022, when the shares closed at least 35% below their previous close. Across all five sell-offs, Rigetti stock fell 52.2% on average, while the S&P 500 fell 12.1%. The other four periods were the 2023 SVB banking crisis, the 2023 five percent yield shock, the 2024 yen unwind and the 2025 US tariff shock.

The stock eventually regained its pre-fall high after all five periods, though not always swiftly. The median wait from the low was 2.5 months, yet two recoveries took more than a year. The longest recovery followed the 2022 fall, requiring 26.1 months until December 2024.

You can't time the next sell-off. You can build for a crash and a rally.

Rigetti Sells More, At Thinner Margins

Rigetti posted revenue of $13.4 million for the twelve months to June 2026, up 68.5% from a year earlier. That figure remains below the $14.4 million recorded over the twelve months to June 2023. Second-quarter revenue reached $5.14 million, up from $1.8 million a year earlier. Management said the second-quarter increase came from sales of its Novera quantum computing systems.

Gross margin has moved the other way. Over twelve-month periods, it fell each year, sliding to 34.6% in the latest period from 81.3% three years earlier. The second quarter of 2026 offered a better result, arriving at 42.6% against 31.4% a year before.

Rigetti held $394 million in cash and short-term investments at the end of June 2026. Counting all of its available-for-sale investments, management put the total at about $541.3 million and said the company operates with no debt. The company recorded a negative $87.6 million in free cash flow over the twelve months to June 2026.

International Business Machines has delivered a 5 year share price that puts a lot of history into today's US$254.32 quote, which raises a simple but hard question for investors: Is the current valuation of IBM really in step with the cash the business is expected to generate over time?

Over the past 5 years, International Business Machines has returned 152.8%, which puts a spotlight on whether the cash flow profile has evolved enough to carry that kind of move.

Fresh announcements around quantum computing, AI infrastructure and enterprise AI security suggest IBM's future investment needs and potential cash generation may shift, which feeds directly into any estimate of what its cash flows are worth today.

Prefer to judge International Business Machines on earnings? See what International Business Machines's 21.5x P/E says about the price.

The issue now is whether IBM's current share price can be fully explained by the cash flows implied by its Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) based intrinsic value estimate.

To pressure test whether IBM's cash flow story feels unique or part of a bigger pattern in AI and quantum infrastructure, line it up against the 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Does International Business Machines Look Undervalued on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here looks at the cash IBM can return to shareholders over time and brings those future dollars back to today. On the latest twelve month view, International Business Machines is generating around $14.0b of free cash flow, and the projections used in this 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity model assume that this pool of cash continues growing rather than shrinking.

Those rising cash flow estimates, combined with a mature profile that still leans into areas like AI infrastructure and quantum computing, lead the DCF model to an intrinsic value that sits meaningfully above the current US$254.32 share price. The launch of IBM's co design platform with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD for quantum error correction helps explain why the model leans on ongoing cash generation, because it ties long term research spending directly to future commercial workloads. That gap between what the cash flows support and where the stock trades is what the full intrinsic worth summary is designed to show in detail.
